§ Key takeaways
01 SIN is required before any paid work in Canada — apply at Service Canada with your study permit. 
02 Study-permit SINs start with "9" and expire with your permit. 
03 In-person service is usually same-day; mail service takes 4–6 weeks. 
04 There is NO fee for a SIN — anyone charging you is running a scam. 
05 Never carry the SIN card in your wallet — memorise the number and store the paper safely. 
The process at a glance
01 Step 1 Gather documents
Original study permit, original passport, and proof of address in Canada (lease, utility bill, or school letter).
02 Step 2 Visit a Service Canada centre
Walk-in or appointment. Bring originals — photocopies are rejected. Closest centre at servicecanada.gc.ca.
03 Step 3 Receive your SIN at the counter
The 9-digit number is printed on a confirmation letter handed to you the same day. No physical card is issued any more.
04 Step 4 Give it to your employer’s payroll
Provide the SIN number plus the expiry date. Employers must re-verify it when your study permit renews.
05 Step 5 Renew the SIN with every permit renewal
Your SIN expiry matches your permit. After PGWP, after PR — return to Service Canada and update the expiry each time.
Overview
This guide provides comprehensive information about canada-sin-number-guide-students for international students in Canada. Understanding Canadian immigration rules is essential for maintaining your study permit status and making informed decisions about your academic and professional future in Canada.
For students from India
Indian-cohort scams often arrive as WhatsApp messages from "consultants" offering fast SINs for INR-equivalent fees. Service Canada walk-in is same-day, free, and bilingual — there is no faster legal channel.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
What government department issues SINs?
A IRCC 
B CRA 
C Service Canada 
D CBSA 
Key Information and Requirements
International students in Canada must comply with their study permit conditions. Key requirements include maintaining full-time enrollment at a designated learning institution (DLI), making satisfactory academic progress, and not working beyond authorized hours. Understanding these conditions is essential for maintaining your status in Canada.
For students from the Philippines
Filipino caregiver-pathway students sometimes inherit a relative’s informal job before getting a SIN. Do not — start dates, hours, and payslips with a SIN are the foundation of every future PGWP and PR claim.
Languages: Filipino (Tagalog) · English (very high proficiency) · Cebuano
Working During Your Studies
International students in Canada can work off campus up to 20 hours per week during academic sessions and full-time during scheduled breaks if their study permit includes this condition. On-campus employment has no hourly limit. Available positions include retail, food service, and research assistant roles at the university.
Working After Graduation
After completing your program, the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) allows you to work in Canada for up to 3 years, depending on your program length. PGWP eligibility requires graduation from a DLI program of at least 8 months. This open work permit allows you to work for any employer in Canada without a job offer requirement.
Pathways to Permanent Residence
Canada offers multiple pathways to permanent residence for international graduates. The Canadian Experience Class (CEC) within Express Entry rewards Canadian education and work experience. Provincial Nominee Programs (PNPs) in many provinces have streams specifically for international graduates of local institutions.
Applying for a SIN as an international student
Apply for a Social Insurance Number through Service Canada with your passport, study permit, and any work authorization documents. A SIN is required for employment and tax reporting. It is not immigration status and does not extend your permit. Keep the SIN confidential; it is an identity number. If your study permit has an expiry date, your SIN record may be tied to that temporary status — update Service Canada when you get a new permit.
“ Your SIN is your tax identity for life — but the number that starts with 9 is a passport stamp, not a card to carry. 
Employers, taxes, and common errors
Give your SIN to legitimate employers and financial institutions when required, not to random housing ads or scholarship scams. File taxes with the Canada Revenue Agency when you have Canadian-source income. If you change names or status, update records promptly. For official steps, use Canada.ca SIN pages rather than third-party form mills.
SIN expiry, renewal, and what happens if it is lost or stolen
A SIN issued with a temporary study permit may carry an expiry date that matches the permit. When you extend your study permit, apply for a SIN renewal with the new permit through Service Canada — your employer needs the updated record for payroll. If your physical SIN confirmation letter is lost or stolen, request a replacement through Service Canada and monitor your credit file for suspicious activity. Do not carry the SIN letter daily; store it with your passport and key immigration documents. If someone uses your SIN fraudulently, report it to Service Canada and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, then place a fraud alert with Equifax and TransUnion.
When the tax year ends and you have worked
If you earned income with your SIN during the tax year, you generally must file a Canadian tax return even as an international student. The CRA uses your SIN to track income slips (T4, T4A) and tuition credits (T2202). Filing on time ensures you receive any refund you are owed — GST/HST credits, climate action incentive payments, or over-deducted tax — and creates a clean record for future immigration applications.

§ Key takeaways
01 Off-campus work cap is 24 hours per week during academic sessions — IRCC raised it from 20 in late 2024. 
02 Full-time work is allowed during scheduled breaks (winter, summer, reading week). 
03 On-campus work has no separate hour cap — but counts against the 24-hour off-campus rule. 
04 You must be a full-time student at an eligible DLI to use off-campus work rights. 
05 A SIN is required before any paid work — apply at Service Canada with your study permit. 
The process at a glance
01 Understand Work Rules Know the work rules for study permit holders
Full-time students at designated learning institutions (DLIs) can work up to 24 hours per week during academic sessions and full-time during scheduled breaks. No separate work permit is needed. Work must stop if you drop to part-time status or take a break from studies.
02 Check Your DLI Verify your school qualifies for off-campus work
Only students at DLIs with a valid designation on IRCCs list can work off-campus. Check your schools DLI status before accepting employment. Schools that lose DLI designation trigger loss of work authorization for their students.
03 Track Hours Carefully Monitor your weekly work hours
The 24-hour cap applies during academic sessions — this is a hard limit across all employers. During scheduled breaks (summer, winter), you can work full-time. Exceeding the 24-hour limit can jeopardize your study permit and future immigration applications.
04 Plan for Transitions Know when work authorization changes
Work authorization ends when you complete your program. PGWP (Post-Graduation Work Permit) provides a transition, but you should apply before your study permit expires. Maintain accurate records of your work hours and employer information.
Overview
For international students in Canada, understanding study permit rules is critical to maintaining lawful status. This comprehensive guide explains canada-study-permit-work-rules in detail, covering eligibility, application procedures, and compliance obligations specific to Canada's immigration system.
For students from India
The 24-hour cap is non-negotiable even when family forex remittance is delayed. If rent is short, talk to your DSO and your school’s financial-aid office about emergency bursaries — do NOT pick up a second cash job to bridge.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
How many hours per week can a study-permit holder work off-campus during the academic session?
A 15 hours 
B 20 hours 
C 24 hours 
D Unlimited 
Key Information and Requirements
Compliance with Canadian study permit conditions requires full-time enrollment at a DLI, regular attendance, and timely reporting of changes to immigration authorities. Understanding your work rights and maintaining proper documentation are essential for a successful stay in Canada.
For students from the Philippines
Remittance flows from Canada back home will be visible to CRA at tax time. Use your SIN-backed payroll job and Wise/CIBC-style traceable transfers — informal "padala" arrangements muddy your work-hours record.
Languages: Filipino (Tagalog) · English (very high proficiency) · Cebuano
Working During Your Studies
Canadian study permit holders can work off campus up to 20 hours per week during regular academic sessions. Full-time work is permitted during scheduled breaks. On-campus employment at your institution has no hourly restrictions. International student advisors can help you understand your specific work authorization.
Working After Graduation
Canadian graduates can transition to the workforce through the PGWP program. This open work permit allows you to gain Canadian work experience, which can support permanent residence applications through programs like Canadian Experience Class. The PGWP is typically issued once per lifetime, so plan its use strategically.
Pathways to Permanent Residence
International students who complete programs in Canada have advantages in the permanent residence process. Canadian educational credentials earn additional CRS points. Canadian work experience through PGWP qualifies candidates for the Canadian Experience Class, one of the most direct pathways to permanent residence.
On-campus and off-campus work conditions
Study permit holders may work on campus and, when eligible, off campus up to the hour limits published by IRCC for their situation. Eligibility can depend on full-time status, program type, and whether the permit states work is allowed. Co-op work may require a separate co-op work permit. Do not start work before you have the correct authorization printed on your permit or in your IRCC account conditions. Hour caps are enforced — track weekly hours across all employers.
“ The 24-hour cap is a hard ceiling — exceed it and you lose more than the job. You can lose your study permit, your PGWP eligibility, and your route to PR. 
SIN, taxes, and status interaction
You need a Social Insurance Number to work. File Canadian tax returns when required, even if you only worked part of the year. If you drop to part-time studies without authorization, work eligibility can end. Before final exams, confirm how post-graduation work permit timing interacts with your last day of study. Use IRCC pages as the controlling rules source; school international offices can explain campus procedures but cannot override IRCC.
Co-op work permits as distinct authorization
A co-op or internship placement that is required by your academic program needs a separate co-op work permit in addition to the study permit — off-campus work authorization alone does not cover it. Apply through IRCC with a letter from your DLI confirming the co-op or internship is an essential program component. Co-op permits are typically free to apply for and are tied to the specific employer and term.

§ Key takeaways
01 File a CRA tax return every year you are in Canada — even with zero income. 
02 Residency for tax (not immigration) is what determines your obligations — most students are tax residents. 
03 GST/HST credit is paid quarterly to low-income tax filers — you must file to claim it. 
04 Tuition is reported on form T2202 and creates carry-forward credits — file even in nil-income years. 
05 Tax deadline is 30 April for most filers; self-employed have until 15 June (taxes still due 30 April). 
The process at a glance
01 Step 1 Confirm tax residency
Most international students with a study permit, Canadian address, and ties (bank, lease, SIN) are deemed tax residents. CRA Form NR74 confirms — your university tax clinic can advise.
02 Step 2 Gather slips
T4 from employers (wages), T4A from scholarships, T2202 from your school (tuition), bank tax slips, and rent receipts (for provincial benefits).
03 Step 3 Pick a filing method
CRA-certified free software (Wealthsimple Tax, TurboTax Free, StudioTax) or a university CVITP volunteer tax clinic for simple returns.
04 Step 4 File by 30 April
Submit via NETFILE for fastest processing. Direct-deposit refunds in 1–2 weeks; paper takes 6–8 weeks.
05 Step 5 Claim GST/HST + provincial credits
These are automatic once you file. The GST/HST credit is paid quarterly (Jul/Oct/Jan/Apr) — typically $300–$500/year for students.
Overview
Studying in Canada as an international student comes with specific rights and responsibilities. This guide provides detailed information about canada-tax-guide-international-students, including eligibility criteria, application timelines, and ongoing requirements.
For students from India
Indian-cohort families often wire tuition mid-year via forex. The remittance itself is NOT taxable income in Canada (it is a gift), but the rupee-to-CAD conversion documentation matters at refund time — keep every forex receipt with your tax file.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
What is the standard tax-filing deadline in Canada for most individuals?
A 15 April 
B 30 April 
C 30 June 
D 31 December 
Key Information and Requirements
As a study permit holder in Canada, you must study full-time at a DLI, progress academically, and comply with all conditions. Your permit specifies whether you can work off campus, and if so, how many hours per week during academic terms.
For students from the Philippines
Money you send home to family ("padala") is NOT tax-deductible in Canada — Canada taxes worldwide income for residents but does not give credits for personal remittances. Budget for the full CAD income to be taxed, not the post-remittance net.
Languages: Filipino (Tagalog) · English (very high proficiency) · Cebuano
Working During Your Studies
Part-time employment helps Canadian international students gain experience and manage living costs. Study permit holders can work up to 20 hours off campus per week during academic sessions. On-campus positions include research assistant, teaching assistant, library, and administrative roles with flexible scheduling.
Working After Graduation
The PGWP is one of the most attractive features of studying in Canada. It gives graduates up to 3 years of open work authorization, during which they can work for any Canadian employer. Canadian work experience gained through the PGWP is highly valued for permanent residence applications.
Pathways to Permanent Residence
Canada's immigration system favors international graduates. The Canadian Experience Class within Express Entry is designed for individuals with Canadian education and work experience. Provincial Nominee Programs offer additional pathways, particularly for graduates who studied and worked in the nominating province.
“ Filing taxes in Canada is not optional for the student who wants PR — your CRA history is the paper trail Express Entry uses to verify every year of work you claim. 
Who must file a Canadian tax return as an international student
An international student in Canada must file a tax return if they: (1) have Canadian-source income (employment, scholarships, bursaries, or grants) and must pay income tax; (2) have tax deducted from income at source and want a refund; (3) qualify for the GST/HST credit or other benefit payments that depend on filing; (4) want to carry forward tuition tax credits (Form T2202) to future tax years. Even if you earned no income at all during the year, filing a return is still advisable because it establishes your tax-filing history and can generate refundable credits. The Canadian tax year is January 1 to December 31, and the filing deadline is April 30 of the following year. If you have self-employment income, the deadline is June 15. File on time even if you owe no tax, because late-filed returns delay benefit payments and can accrue penalties if you later have a balance owing. Use CRA-certified tax software or a free community volunteer tax clinic rather than unregulated online preparers.
Form T2202 tuition tax credit: how it works and why it matters
Your DLI issues a Form T2202 or TL11A tuition and enrolment certificate each February for the preceding calendar year. The certificate shows the eligible tuition fees you paid during the year. This amount generates a non-refundable tax credit — it reduces the income tax you owe but cannot create a refund if you have no tax liability. Unused tuition credits carry forward indefinitely to any future year. For students with low or no income during their studies, filing a tax return to report the T2202 is essential: the carried-forward credits can offset thousands of dollars in tax liability once you start working full-time after graduation. body:

Changing from F-2 to F-1 Visa: Process and Requirements 
Skip to main content MyCaseworks 
Home

Your stats 
Following

§ Key takeaways
01 F-2 → F-1 change of status requires full-time admission to a SEVP-certified school and a new I-20. 
02 File Form I-539 with USCIS, or depart the US and apply for an F-1 visa at a consulate (often faster). 
03 I-539 processing typically runs 2–6 months — you cannot start full-time study until approved. 
04 Pay the SEVIS I-901 fee ($350 as of 2026) separately as part of the change. 
05 Keep maintaining F-2 status throughout — full-time spousal study and any unauthorised work both terminate F-2 retroactively. 
The process at a glance
01 Step 1 Get accepted to a SEVP school
Apply early — universities often issue I-20s only after deposit. SEVP certification is at studyinthestates.dhs.gov.
02 Step 2 Receive a new F-1 I-20
The school’s DSO issues an I-20 in your name with "change of status" notation. Pay tuition deposit and provide funding evidence.
03 Step 3 Pay the SEVIS I-901 fee
Pay online at fmjfee.com using the SEVIS ID on the new I-20. Keep the receipt — required for the I-539 packet AND any consular processing.
04 Step 4 Choose pathway
Option A: File Form I-539 inside the US (slow but no travel). Option B: Depart the US, apply for F-1 visa at consulate, re-enter on F-1 (faster but riskier in case of denial).
05 Step 5 Wait for approval and start study
Do not start full-time enrolment until USCIS approves I-539 or you re-enter on F-1. Premature full-time enrolment terminates F-2.
Overview
Navigating family immigration as an F-1 student requires understanding how dependent status works in the US immigration system. This guide explains changing-from-f2-to-f1-visa in detail, helping you plan for your family's arrival and ensure everyone maintains valid status throughout your program.
For families from India
Indian-cohort F-2 spouses sometimes deplete the family savings on the change to F-1, only to find tuition is twice what was planned. Run the full 2-year cost in advance: tuition, fees, separate health-insurance premium, and a 6-month emergency fund.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
Which form does an F-2 dependent file to change status to F-1 inside the US?
A Form I-20 only 
B Form I-539 (Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status) 
C Form I-765 
D Form I-485 
Eligibility Requirements
To qualify for F-2 visas, the F-1 student must maintain full-time enrollment and good academic standing. Each dependent submits their own application with evidence of the family relationship. Financial documentation must show adequate resources for all dependents without relying on unauthorized employment.
For families from China
Chinese-cohort F-2 → F-1 applicants face higher 221(g) administrative-processing rates at consular re-entry for STEM fields. If the consular route is chosen, budget 4–8 weeks for security checks before booking flights back.
Languages: Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) · Cantonese
§ Test your knowledge
Why would F-2 → F-1 via consular processing be faster than I-539?
A Consulates do not require an I-20 
B I-539 USCIS processing currently runs 2–6 months; a consular F-1 visa interview can be scheduled within weeks 
C Consular fees are lower 
D Consular F-1 visas are exempt from SEVIS 
Application Process for Dependents
The F-2 visa application process requires careful attention to documentation and timing. Each dependent submits their own DS-160, pays the fee, and schedules an interview. After approval, dependents receive an F-2 visa allowing them to enter the US with or shortly after the student.
§ Test your knowledge
You filed I-539 in January. Can you start full-time MBA classes in March?
A Yes — filing counts as approval 
B No — full-time enrolment must wait for I-539 approval or you must re-enter on F-1 
C Yes — if the DSO confirms 
D Only if also enrolled part-time 
Rights and Restrictions for F-2 Dependents
F-2 dependents have limited rights. The most significant restriction is the prohibition on employment for both paid and unpaid work. Dependents may study part-time for recreational purposes. Children may attend US schools full-time through grade 12.
Financial Planning for Families
The cost of supporting a family while studying is significantly higher. Budget for family-sized housing, food for multiple people, dependent health insurance, and children's school supplies. Some universities offer subsidized family housing and insurance plans.
“ F-2 to F-1 is not a paperwork step — it is a status reset. New I-20, new SEVIS fee, new visa stamp eventually. Plan it like a fresh admission. 
Change of status within the US vs consular processing abroad
An F-2 dependent who has been admitted to a US degree program can either: (1) file Form I-539 (Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status) within the US to change from F-2 to F-1 status without leaving the country; or (2) depart the US and apply for an F-1 visa at a US embassy or consulate abroad. Filing for change of status within the US has the advantage that you do not need to interrupt your residence or travel — you remain in F-2 status while the I-539 is pending and maintain lawful presence. The disadvantage is that the current USCIS processing time for I-539 is 6-12 months, and you cannot begin F-1 studies until the F-1 approval is granted. If you apply at the consulate abroad, you receive the F-1 visa faster (typically 2-8 weeks from interview), but you must depart the US and re-enter after the visa is issued. If you are from a country with high visa refusal rates, I-539 within the US avoids the consular visa refusal risk. Choose the option that matches your timeline: if the program starts soon, consular processing may be the only workable path. If you have time to wait, I-539 is safer.

03 Authorisation appears on page 2 of your I-20 — employer name, dates, full-time/part-time. No EAD card. 
04 Part-time CPT (≤20 hours/week) does NOT count against OPT; full-time CPT 12+ months ELIMINATES OPT. 
05 Every job change needs a new I-20 with updated CPT block — work starts on the new start date listed, not before. 
The process at a glance
01 Step 1 Identify the qualifying course
The internship must be tied to a course that grants academic credit OR be a required degree component (co-op, practicum). Talk to your academic advisor before approaching your DSO.
02 Step 2 Secure the offer letter
Get a written offer on company letterhead: job title, start/end dates, weekly hours, salary, supervisor, address, and a description tying duties to your major.
03 Step 3 Submit CPT request to DSO
Use your school’s portal. Attach offer letter, course registration, and any required academic-advisor approval. Allow 1–2 weeks processing.
04 Step 4 Receive new I-20
Your DSO updates SEVIS and prints a new I-20 with CPT authorisation on page 2. The dates on the I-20 are the legal employment window — no day earlier, no day later.
05 Step 5 Complete the course
You must actually finish the linked course and submit any required reflection paper/evaluation. Skipping the academic component retroactively makes the CPT unauthorised.
Overview
Work authorization is one of the most important topics for F-1 students planning to gain professional experience in the US. This guide walks through curricular-practical-training-cpt-guide step by step, from eligibility to maintaining compliance after approval.
For students from India
Many Indian-cohort students treat the summer between MS year 1 and year 2 as the CPT season. Confirm with your DSO that your school has a summer internship course; some require pre-registration in spring or you will miss the window entirely.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
Who authorises CPT?
A USCIS — by approving Form I-765 
B Your DSO — by issuing an updated I-20 
C The Department of Labor — via LCA filing 
D Your employer’s HR team 
Eligibility and Key Requirements
F-1 work eligibility begins after completing one academic year. Your DSO must confirm your status and recommend you in SEVIS. Each work option has specific requirements: CPT needs a job offer, OPT needs a completed degree, and STEM OPT needs an E-Verified employer.
For students from China
Chinese-cohort students sometimes do unpaid lab CPT under a faculty supervisor. Get this on the I-20 anyway — unpaid + academic still counts as employment for F-1 purposes, and the I-20 is your protection at any future visa stamping.
Languages: Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) · Cantonese
Application Process and Timelines
Each F-1 work authorization type has a different process. OPT: Form I-765 filed 90 days before to 60 days after program end. CPT: authorized by DSO before starting work. On-campus: requires securing a qualifying position. Maintain copies of all documents.
Maintaining Compliance and Reporting
Compliance involves maintaining F-1 status and following specific work rules. Continue full-time enrollment, keep your passport and I-94 valid, and report changes promptly. For CPT and OPT, ensure employment relates to your field and document your hours and responsibilities.
Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
Avoid mistakes by preparing carefully. Common errors include unsigned forms, incorrect fees, missing documents, and filing outside the window. Create a checklist and review with your DSO. After approval, avoid compliance mistakes like unreported address changes and unauthorized work.
“ CPT is academic credit that happens to be paid — not paid work that happens to be academic. The credit comes first. 
CPT eligibility: the one-academic-year rule and exceptions
Federal regulations require F-1 students to complete one full academic year (typically two semesters or three quarters) before being eligible for CPT. The exception is for graduate students whose programs require immediate CPT participation — for example, a summer internship that is mandatory before the first fall semester. Even in these cases, the DSO must record a specific note in SEVIS explaining why the early CPT is integral to the curriculum. Part-time CPT (20 hours or fewer per week) is authorized separately from full-time CPT and does not affect OPT eligibility. Full-time CPT (over 20 hours per week) must be authorized with the understanding that 12 months or more of full-time CPT eliminates OPT eligibility at the same degree level. CPT is authorized on a semester-by-semester or term-by-term basis; a single CPT authorization cannot span multiple semesters unless the DSO enters separate authorizations for each term.
How to get CPT authorized: the DSO process and employer letter requirements
To obtain CPT, you must: (1) register for a course that requires or permits off-campus work — an internship, practicum, cooperative education, or independent study that integrates the work experience into the curriculum; (2) obtain a job offer letter from the employer that includes your job title, start and end dates, number of hours per week, a detailed description of duties, and the employer’s name and address; (3) submit a CPT request through your DSO, typically via the international office’s online portal or a paper form. The DSO will verify that the job relates to your major field of study, that you have met the one-academic-year waiting period, and that the CPT dates align with the course enrollment period. 02 On-campus employment is allowed up to 20 hours per week during semesters and full-time during breaks. After one academic year, CPT and OPT provide off-campus work authorisation.

The process at a glance
01 Apply & I-20 Receive your I-20 from the university
After accepting your admission offer and providing proof of financial resources, the university's international student office issues your Form I-20. Verify all details on the I-20 match your passport — name spelling errors can cause visa delays. Keep the I-20 with your passport at all times during your stay in the US.
02 Visa Interview Apply for your F-1 student visa
Complete Form DS-160 online, pay the SEVIS I-901 fee ($350), and schedule a visa interview at the US embassy or consulate in your home country. Prepare documents: passport, I-20, DS-160 confirmation, SEVIS fee receipt, financial evidence, admission letter, academic transcripts, and standardised test scores. Be prepared to explain your study plans and ties to your home country.
03 Arrive & Register Arrive in the US and check in with the international office
Arrive no earlier than 30 days before your programme start date. Attend the mandatory international student orientation where you will learn about SEVIS compliance, health insurance requirements, campus safety, and available support services. Complete check-in with the international student office to activate your SEVIS record.
04 Settle In Open a bank account, get a US phone, and find housing
Open a US bank account (checking and savings) using your passport and I-20. Get a US phone number — prepaid plans are available without a Social Security Number. If living on campus, confirm your housing assignment and move-in date. If off campus, finalise your lease, set up utilities, and arrange transportation to campus.
05 Plan Career Start career planning from your first semester
Visit the career centre early to understand OPT timelines, build your resume, and learn about on-campus recruiting. Many international students find that building faculty relationships leads to research assistant positions and strong recommendation letters. Attend career fairs and networking events specifically for international students.
About Dallas College
Located in Dallas, TX, Dallas College is a community college that welcomes international students seeking quality US education at an affordable price. The college offers associate degree programs and transfer options designed to help students progress to bachelor's degree programs.
For students from India
Indian students should begin the credential evaluation process early — many US universities require WES evaluation of Indian transcripts. Connect with the Indian Students Association at your university for academic support, cultural events, and professional networking. For funding, explore education loans from SBI, HDFC, and ICICI that offer collateral-free options for students admitted to US universities. The US consulates in India (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata) have varying F-1 visa interview wait times — apply early, especially during the summer peak.

Starting at {name} allows international students to complete prerequisite courses at a lower cost before transferring.

Day 1 CPT vs Regular CPT: Rules, Risks, and Best Practices

§ Key takeaways
01 Regular CPT requires one full academic year of US enrolment before authorisation; Day 1 CPT does not. 
02 Day 1 CPT schools authorise work from the first day of enrolment — high USCIS scrutiny, high audit risk. 
03 CPT must be integral to your curriculum and tied to academic credit, regardless of which model your school uses. 
04 12 months or more of full-time CPT eliminates your post-completion OPT eligibility — permanently. 
05 A "Day 1 CPT degree" with no in-person instruction is a red flag at consular interviews and adjustment-of-status. 
The process at a glance
01 Understand CPT Know the difference between Day 1 CPT and regular CPT
Day 1 CPT allows immediate work authorization from day one of a program, while regular CPT requires one academic year of study. Day 1 CPT is legal but high-risk — USCIS scrutinizes these programs closely. Only use it at universities with legitimate in-person curricula, not CPT mills.
02 Check Eligibility Verify your academic program qualifies for CPT
CPT must be an integral part of your curriculum. You need a job offer letter, a signed CPT recommendation from your DSO, and enrollment in a CPT-authorized course. Day 1 CPT requires your employer to certify the work is directly related to your field of study.
03 Assess Risks Evaluate the visa and immigration risks
Day 1 CPT carries higher RFE risk during H-1B or green card processing. USCIS may question whether you entered the program primarily for work authorization. Maintain full-time enrollment, attend classes in person, and keep all CPT documentation for future applications.
04 Apply Strategically Submit CPT application through your DSO
Submit your CPT application with your job offer, employer letter, and academic justification. Day 1 CPT requires special authorization — ensure your DSO understands your program structure. Processing takes 5-10 business days. Renew CPT each semester.
Overview
Work authorization is one of the most important topics for F-1 students planning to gain professional experience in the US. This guide walks through day-1-cpt-vs-regular-cpt step by step, from eligibility to maintaining compliance after approval.
For students from India
Indian-cohort applicants are over-represented in Day 1 CPT programmes — and over-represented in subsequent USCIS denials. If you go this route, do a US in-person residency for at least the first term, keep boarding passes, lecture notes, and graded assignments as evidence.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
What is the core legal difference between Day 1 CPT and regular CPT?
A Day 1 CPT is approved by USCIS; regular CPT is not 
B Day 1 CPT skips the one-academic-year wait that regular CPT requires 
C Day 1 CPT is only available to STEM students 
D There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable 
Eligibility and Key Requirements
F-1 work eligibility begins after completing one academic year. Your DSO must confirm your status and recommend you in SEVIS. Each work option has specific requirements: CPT needs a job offer, OPT needs a completed degree, and STEM OPT needs an E-Verified employer.
Application Process and Timelines
Each F-1 work authorization type has a different process. OPT: Form I-765 filed 90 days before to 60 days after program end. CPT: authorized by DSO before starting work. On-campus: requires securing a qualifying position. Maintain copies of all documents.
Maintaining Compliance and Reporting
Compliance involves maintaining F-1 status and following specific work rules. Continue full-time enrollment, keep your passport and I-94 valid, and report changes promptly. For CPT and OPT, ensure employment relates to your field and document your hours and responsibilities.
Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
Avoid mistakes by preparing carefully. Common errors include unsigned forms, incorrect fees, missing documents, and filing outside the window. Create a checklist and review with your DSO. After approval, avoid compliance mistakes like unreported address changes and unauthorized work.
“ Day 1 CPT is not illegal — but it is the riskiest legal path. The school authorises it; USCIS judges it later. 
What makes CPT "regular" vs "Day 1" and why the distinction matters
Curricular Practical Training (CPT) is an F-1 benefit that authorizes off-campus employment that is an integral part of the school’s curriculum. Regular CPT is typically available after one academic year of full-time enrollment and requires a specific course enrollment (internship, practicum, cooperative education) that integrates the work into the academic program. Day 1 CPT — where a school authorizes CPT from the first day of enrollment — is a practice that USCIS and immigration attorneys treat with caution. Day 1 CPT programs are most common at private universities offering what are sometimes called “CPT-friendly” or “CPT-for-day-one” programs. The key legal issue is whether the CPT is genuinely curricular (required by the program) or merely a work authorization scheme circumventing the one-academic-year waiting period mandated by regulation. If USCIS determines the CPT was not bona fide, the student may face status violations, OPT denial, or even findings of inadmissibility.
The 12-month full-time CPT rule and its effect on OPT eligibility
Federal regulations state that 12 months or more of full-time CPT eliminates eligibility for post-completion OPT at the same degree level. Part-time CPT (20 hours or fewer per week) does not count toward this limit. This means a student who uses 12+ months of full-time CPT during a master’s program cannot apply for OPT after completing that master’s degree. The process at a glance
01 Check Eligibility Verify you can bring dependants
Only PhD/research postgraduate students and government-sponsored students can bring dependants in 2026. Check your CAS Tier field: it must show "PGR" (Postgraduate Research) or your scholarship letter must confirm government sponsorship.
02 Prepare Funds Proof of maintenance for each dependant
UKVI expects £845/month outside London or £1,083/month inside London for each dependant, multiplied by up to 9 months. Funds must have been in your account for 28 consecutive days. Scholarships or official sponsorship letters can substitute.
03 Apply Online Submit separate dependant application
Each dependant submits their own online application via gov.uk. Pay the visa fee (£490) and IHS surcharge (£1,035/year per dependant).
04 Receive Visa Travel and register in the UK
Dependant visa processing typically takes 3-8 weeks. Priority processing (£500) cuts this to 5 working days. Dependants can arrive before or after the main applicant. Upon arrival, the spouse dependant can work full-time in any role immediately — no skill threshold.
Overview
This guide explains how dependants of UK Student visa holders apply and stay compliant under current Home Office rules. Dependant eligibility depends on the main applicant’s course level, start date, and sponsorship category. Always verify the latest GOV.UK Student visa family guidance before you budget housing or file, because taught postgraduate dependant rules tightened in recent policy cycles.
For students from India
Indian-cohort PhD applicants are the largest user of the dependant route post-2024. Keep the 28-day funds-seasoning rule in mind: parental forex remittance must land in your account at least 28 days before the application date, and the closing balance on every day in that window must stay above the threshold.

If the main course no longer permits dependants, do not file a futile application — re-check GOV.UK first.
For students from Nigeria
Nigerian applicants frequently get refused on dependant funds because of FX-conversion timing. Convert and deposit naira-to-GBP early, then keep one currency throughout the 28-day window — UKVI will not blend balances across currencies, and any dip below the threshold restarts the clock.

02 EB-1A (extraordinary ability) and EB-1B (outstanding researcher) allow self- or employer-petition without labour cert. 
03 Most graduate students take EB-2 (advanced degree) or EB-3 (skilled worker) — both require labour certification. 
04 EB-2 NIW (National Interest Waiver) skips the labour cert if you can prove your work is in the US national interest. 
05 India and China face decades-long EB-2/EB-3 backlogs due to per-country quotas; EB-1 is the only realistic relief. 
The process at a glance
01 Step 1 Build employer + degree fit
Most EB-2/EB-3 cases need a US employer willing to sponsor. Choose roles and companies with proven I-140 history.
02 Step 2 PERM labour certification
Employer files ETA-9089 with DOL. Prevailing wage determination + recruitment campaign + final filing. Usually 6–12 months.
03 Step 3 File I-140
Employer files Form I-140 (Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers). Approval establishes your priority date.
04 Step 4 Wait for visa availability
Check the monthly Visa Bulletin. For India/China EB-2/EB-3, expect 6–15+ year waits as of 2026.
05 Step 5 File I-485 or consular processing
Adjustment of status (I-485) inside the US, or DS-260 consular processing abroad. Final step to permanent resident.
Overview
For F-1 international students, understanding work authorization rules is critical to maintaining lawful status. This comprehensive guide explains f1-eb1-visa-for-graduate-students in detail, covering eligibility, application procedures, and compliance obligations.
For students from India
Indian-born applicants face the worst EB-2/EB-3 backlogs of any country. Strategy: file the I-140 ASAP for the priority date, then continue building the EB-1B case (citations, peer reviews, original contributions). Cross-chargeability to a non-Indian-born spouse can shave years.

What is the typical immigration sequence from F-1 to US permanent residence?
A F-1 → green card directly via Form I-485 
B F-1 → OPT → H-1B → I-140 → I-485 or consular processing 
C F-1 → marriage → green card automatically 
D F-1 → 5 years of presence → automatic citizenship 
Eligibility and Key Requirements
To be eligible, F-1 students must maintain valid immigration status throughout the process. This means full-time enrollment, no unauthorized employment history, and SEVIS compliance. Your DSO plays a crucial role in verifying eligibility and initiating work authorization applications.
For students from China
Chinese-born EB-2 backlog is shorter than Indian but still significant. Faculty roles plus academic publications make EB-1B (outstanding researcher) realistic — fast-track for tenure-track PhD graduates. PERM is not required for EB-1.

Application Process and Timelines
The work authorization process involves steps in the correct order. Your DSO recommends you in SEVIS and issues an endorsed I-20. Then compile your application package and submit within the designated window. Track progress through your USCIS online account.
Maintaining Compliance and Reporting
After approval, ongoing compliance is essential. Report address changes within 10 days, stay within authorized hours, and keep your SEVIS record active. For OPT participants, unemployment days count against your authorized period, so track employment status carefully.
Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
The most costly mistakes include missing filing deadlines, exceeding unemployment limits, and accepting unauthorized employment. These errors jeopardize your application and F-1 status. Understand rules thoroughly, maintain a compliance calendar, and seek professional guidance.
“ The H-1B is a six-year transit lounge. Your priority date is your boarding pass — get one as soon as possible. 
Mapping the F-1 to green card timeline: OPT, H-1B, and employment-based immigration
The transition from F-1 to permanent resident typically follows a multi-step path: F-1 → OPT (12 months) → STEM OPT extension (24 months for STEM graduates) → H-1B (up to 6 years) → PERM labor certification → I-140 immigrant petition → adjustment of status or consular processing. Each step has its own timelines, costs, and risks. The OPT-to-H-1B bridge depends on the H-1B lottery: without selection, you may exhaust OPT and need to enrol in a new program, use cap-exempt H-1B, or depart the US. Once the I-140 is approved (and if you are from a country with no visa backlog), you can file for adjustment of status concurrently. If you are from India or China, per-country visa backlogs mean you may wait years or decades between I-140 approval and adjustment eligibility. Planning for the backlog is critical — your H-1B status can be extended beyond 6 years once the I-140 has been pending for 365+ days or has been approved and a priority date is current in the Final Action Date chart only after a multi-year wait.
PERM labor certification: what employers need to prove and how long it takes
Most employment-based green cards (EB-2 and EB-3 categories) require the employer to obtain a PERM labor certification from the Department of Labor before the I-140 can be filed. The PERM process requires the employer to (1) test the US labor market by posting the job in multiple channels (job boards, newspapers, internal postings, state workforce agency) for at least 30 days; (2) recruit in good faith for the role; (3) demonstrate that no qualified, willing, and available US worker applied for the position; (4) file the ETA-9089 form with the DOL. The recruitment step takes 60-90 days to complete, and DOL processing of the PERM application currently takes 8-12 months. After PERM is cert

§ Key takeaways
01 F-1 students may work on-campus up to 20 hours/week during term and full-time during breaks — no separate authorisation. 
02 Off-campus work requires CPT, OPT, severe economic hardship, or international-organisation employment authorisation. 
03 Self-employment, freelance gigs, and "side hustles" are off-limits unless an EAD specifically permits it. 
04 Unauthorised employment terminates F-1 status retroactively and triggers unlawful-presence accrual. 
05 Reinstatement after unauthorised work is discretionary and rarely granted — prevention is far cheaper. 
The process at a glance
01 Know the Rules Understand F-1 employment categories
F-1 students have three work authorization paths: on-campus (20 hrs/week during semesters), CPT (authorized internship during studies), and OPT (pre/post-completion work authorization). Each has specific rules, timelines, and application procedures. Working outside these categories violates your status.
02 On-Campus Work Apply for on-campus employment
On-campus jobs (library, dining, research assistant) are automatically authorized with your F-1 status — no separate application needed. You can work up to 20 hours/week during the academic year and full-time during breaks. Find positions through your universitys career portal.
03 Apply for CPT Get Curricular Practical Training authorization
CPT requires one academic year of study (except grad programs requiring immediate CPT). You need a job offer, a signed CPT recommendation from your DSO, and CPT course enrollment. CPT can be part-time or full-time. Over 12 months of full-time CPT eliminates OPT eligibility.
04 Plan for OPT Apply for Optional Practical Training
OPT allows 12 months of work authorization (36 months for STEM). Apply up to 90 days before your program end date. USCIS processing takes 3-5 months. You need a job in your field of study. STEM OPT requires an employer enrolled in E-Verify.
Overview
Navigating work authorization as an F-1 student requires careful attention to regulations and deadlines. This guide covers the key aspects of f1-visa-employment-restrictions, helping you understand your options, obligations, and compliance requirements.
For students from Nigeria
Currency volatility means tuition bills look impossible some semesters. Severe-economic-hardship EAD is a real (if narrow) option — but never take cash hustles to bridge the gap; one unauthorised week can void four years of investment.
Languages: English (official) · Yoruba · Igbo · Hausa
§ Test your knowledge
What is the maximum on-campus working hours for F-1 students during the academic term?
A 10 hours/week 
B 20 hours/week 
C 30 hours/week 
D There is no limit 
Eligibility and Key Requirements
Eligibility depends on your enrollment status, type of employment, and academic progress. You must maintain full-time enrollment, be in good standing, and have your DSO's SEVIS recommendation. For CPT and OPT, employment must be directly related to your field of study.
For students from India
Indian-cohort students sometimes take freelance development gigs for clients back home and assume "the money never enters the US" makes it safe. USCIS treats work done while physically present in the US as US employment — regardless of where the client or money lives.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
Application Process and Timelines
Applying for work authorization requires careful attention to filing windows and documentation. Each application type has specific forms, fees, and supporting documents. Start gathering documents early and plan your application timeline accordingly to maintain valid status while pending.
Maintaining Compliance and Reporting
Maintaining compliance is as important as the application. Continue meeting F-1 requirements including full-time enrollment and timely reporting. For OPT and STEM OPT, submit periodic validation reports and update employer details promptly. Non-compliance can terminate your authorization.
Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
Common mistakes include using outdated forms, incorrect fee amounts, missing signatures, and inconsistent information. Use the latest USCIS forms, double-check fees, and review your application before submission. Working with your DSO catches many common errors before filing.
“ There is no grey area in F-1 employment. Either you have written authorisation, or you do not work — full stop. 
On-campus, CPT, OPT, and what counts as unauthorized work
F-1 students may work on campus up to 20 hours per week while school is in session and full-time during official breaks, subject to school policy and a valid I-20. Off-campus work generally requires CPT (during the program, authorized by the DSO) or OPT (USCIS employment authorization). Remote work for a foreign employer while physically in the United States can still be unauthorized if it is employment performed in the US without the correct authorization. Gig work, freelancing, and unpaid roles that replace a US worker can also violate status. When in doubt, get written guidance from your DSO before you start. Unauthorized employment can make you ineligible for benefits such as reinstatement, change of status, or future visas.
Incident response if you already worked without authorization
If you discover you performed unauthorized work, stop immediately and speak with your DSO. Document the dates, hours, employer, and nature of the work. Do not destroy records. Depending on severity and timing, options may include continuing on status if the issue is minor and corrected, seeking reinstatement after a status violation, or departing and re-entering with a clean plan. Never rely on informal advice from classmates or employers. For high-stakes cases — especially those involving SEVIS termination or a pending green-card

03 Marrying another non-immigrant (F-1, H-1B) does NOT automatically grant work authorisation or green card.

The process at a glance
01 Understand Marriage Rules Know how marriage affects F-1 status
Getting married while on F-1 status does not automatically change your immigration status. F-1 students remain on F-1 after marriage. Your spouse can apply for F-2 dependent status. Marrying a US citizen or green card holder opens the door to green card sponsorship.
02 Apply for F-2 Spouse Get F-2 status for your new spouse
Your spouse needs their own I-20 and F-2 visa application. Request an F-2 I-20 from your DSO showing sufficient financial support for two people. If your spouse is already in the US, they may be able to file a change of status rather than leaving for a visa interview.
03 Consider Adjustment If marrying a US citizen, explore green card options
Marriage to a US citizen allows the F-1 student to apply for a marriage-based green card. This is a separate process from F-1 status — consult an immigration attorney. Filing I-130 and I-485 (adjustment of status) while maintaining F-1 status requires careful planning.
04 Maintain F-1 Compliance Keep your F-1 status valid during and after marriage
Marriage does not excuse you from F-1 requirements. Continue full-time enrollment, maintain valid I-20, and follow all F-1 rules. If pursuing a green card through marriage, do not assume F-1 rules no longer apply until the green card is approved.
Overview
International students who wish to bring their family to the US need to understand the dependent visa process thoroughly. This guide provides comprehensive information about f1-visa-marriage-during-studies, including eligibility criteria, application steps, financial requirements, and rights for F-2 dependent visa holders.
For students from India
Indian-cohort weddings often pre-date the US move — keep wedding photos with dates, mandap and groom-side family included, plus a certified English translation of the Indian marriage certificate. USCIS expects documentary continuity, not just a US courthouse certificate.

Rights and Restrictions for F-2 Dependents

“ Marriage is a status change, not a status upgrade. The F-1 study commitment continues until USCIS adjusts your status — or terminates it.

Marrying a US citizen while in F-1 status does not automatically change your status — you remain an F-1 student until you file for adjustment of status through the I-130/I-485 process. Many F-1 students marry a US citizen during their studies and continue on F-1 status through graduation, then adjust status after OPT or directly after marrying. 02 Each dependent files Form DS-160 separately and attends the consular interview (children under 14 often waived). 
03 You must show extra funds for every dependent — universities estimate $5,000–$10,000 per dependent per year. 
04 F-2 dependents cannot work in the US — there is no F-2 EAD pathway.

The process at a glance
01 Check Eligibility Verify requirements for F-2 dependent status
F-2 status is available to the spouse and unmarried children under 21 of F-1 students. You must prove the F-1 student has sufficient financial resources to support dependents. Each dependent needs their own Form I-20 and SEVIS record.
02 Apply for Status Submit the F-2 visa application
The F-1 student requests an F-2 I-20 from their DSO for each dependent. Dependents apply for F-2 visas at a US consulate with the I-20, proof of relationship (marriage certificate, birth certificates), financial documents, and valid passports. Processing times vary by consulate.
03 Understand Restrictions Know what F-2 status allows and prohibits
F-2 dependents cannot work in the US under any circumstances. Spouses can study part-time recreationally (not toward a degree). Children can attend public K-12 school full-time. Full-time degree study requires changing to F-1 status. Plan financially assuming one income.
04 Maintain Status Keep your F-2 status valid
F-2 status is dependent on the F-1 student maintaining their status. If the F-1 student drops below full-time, graduates, or violates status, F-2 status ends simultaneously. File for a change of status or plan departure before the F-1 program ends.
Overview
Bringing your family to the US while studying on an F-1 visa involves a separate immigration process for each dependent. This guide provides detailed information about f2-dependent-visa-spouse-children, covering requirements, timelines, and financial considerations.
For families from India
Indian-cohort spouses often arrive intending to "study part-time and work later" — but only the F-1 conversion makes work possible. Plan the F-2 → F-1 change as a 6–9 month process and budget for separate F-1 tuition.

04 No SEVIS fee is paid by F-2 dependents — they share the F-1 student’s SEVIS record. 
05 Universities issue separate F-2 I-20s; some schools list dependents on the F-1 student’s portal. 
The process at a glance
01 Understand F-2 Study Limits Know what study is allowed on F-2
F-2 dependents can study part-time for recreation or enrichment, but cannot pursue a full-time degree program. Recreational study includes individual courses, language classes, and non-credit certifications. Full-time degree study requires changing to F-1 status.
02 Explore Part-Time Options Find study options within F-2 rules
Look for: non-credit certificate programs, language learning courses, online classes, community education, and auditing university courses. Many universities allow F-2 spouses to audit classes or take non-degree courses that do not lead to a full degree.
03 Plan F-1 Transition Prepare to change from F-2 to F-1 for degree study
To pursue a full degree, you must change status from F-2 to F-1. This requires: admission to a SEVP-certified school, proof of financial support, a new I-20, and filing Form I-539 with USCIS. Processing takes 3-8 months — plan ahead and maintain valid status during the transition.
04 Time Your Transition Coordinate with the F-1 students program timeline
Changing to F-1 means both you and your spouse are on separate F-1 statuses. Plan the transition so it does not conflict with your spouses graduation or OPT timeline. Consider consulting an immigration attorney for complex family situations.
Overview
For F-1 students planning to bring their spouse and children to the United States, understanding the dependent visa process is essential. This guide covers f2-visa-study-options, from initial application through maintaining status and financial planning.
For families from India
Many Indian-cohort spouses arrive intending to "wait it out" on F-2. Use the time productively — part-time English, professional certifications, GMAT prep — so the F-1 change-of-status case looks like a clear academic plan, not a workaround.

§ Test your knowledge
F-2 spouse wants to enrol full-time in an MBA. What status do they need?
A F-2 is fine — full-time study is allowed 
B Must change status to F-1 (and pay separate tuition + SEVIS fee) 
C Must enrol in H-4 status 
D Only J-1 status allows MBA study 
Eligibility Requirements
F-2 eligibility is directly tied to the F-1 student's status. Spouses and unmarried children under 21 may qualify. Requirements include proof of relationship, evidence of the student's valid F-1 status, and comprehensive financial documentation for the entire family.
Application Process for Dependents
Dependents can apply for visas at the same time as the student or after the student has received theirs. Each dependent needs their own DS-160 confirmation, fee receipt, and interview appointment. Financial documents must show sufficient resources for the entire family.
Rights and Restrictions for F-2 Dependents
The F-2 visa allows spouses and children to live in the US but with limited activities. Spouses cannot work and can only study part-time in non-degree programs. Children can attend US public schools without a separate student visa.
“ F-2 lets you build skills part-time, not finish a degree. To finish, you need F-1 — plan for the change of status from day one. 
Financial Planning for Families
F-1 students with dependents should plan for $15,000 to $25,000 in additional annual expenses per dependent. Largest costs are housing, food, and health insurance. Explore on-campus employment and scholarships that consider family circumstances.
Part-time recreational study: what qualifies and how to enrol
F-2 visa holders may engage in study that is recreational or avocational in nature — courses that are not part of a full-time degree program and do not lead to a certificate or diploma that would qualify as a full-time academic credential. Examples include a single art class at a community college, a language course at a non-degree programme, dance or music lessons, a continuing education workshop, or an online certificate through a non-degree platform. The key limitation is that the study must not be full-time and must not lead to a certificate or diploma. Enrolling in a full-time associate degree program or a full-time English as a Second Language program would typically violate F-2 study conditions. If the F-2 holder later wants to pursue a full-time degree, they must apply for a change of status to F-1 before enrolling. The application for change of status requires a new I-20 from the school, proof of financial support, and a nonimmigrant intent statement showing ties to the home country. During the change-of-status processing period, the applicant may begin study only after the F-1 approval notice is issued — not before.
Children’s K-12 education and transitioning to F-1 for college
F-2 dependent children are permitted to attend any US K-12 school — public or private — full-time without needing their own visa. Public K-12 school attendance is allowed for the duration of the F-1 parent’s authorized stay. For children approaching college age (grade 11 or 12), plan the transition to F-1 status: the college-bound child must apply to US universities as an international student, obtain a Form I-20, and apply for F-1 visa or change of status before starting full-time degree studies. § Key takeaways
01 F-2 dependents cannot work in the US — paid or unpaid, on-campus or off, remote or in person. 
02 There is no F-2 EAD pathway — unlike H-4 dependents of H-1B holders. 
03 Self-employment, freelance, gig work, and remote work for non-US clients are all banned on F-2 status. 
04 To work, F-2 must change status to F-1 (and use CPT/OPT) or to a working visa like H-1B/L-1. 
05 Volunteering at a true non-profit in unpaid-norm roles is the only exception — same test as for F-1 students. 
The process at a glance
01 Understand F-2 Rules Know that F-2 dependents cannot work
F-2 visa holders are strictly prohibited from working in the US — there is no exception for remote work, freelance, or unpaid positions. Any work, including for a foreign employer while physically in the US, violates F-2 status. Even volunteering at a for-profit company may be considered work.
02 Explore Alternatives Consider changing to work-authorized status
If you need work authorization, options include: changing to F-1 status (study), H-1B (if sponsored by employer), or green card through family sponsorship. F-2 to F-1 change of status is common but requires admission to a school and proof of funds.
03 Avoid Violations Recognize activities that violate F-2 work rules
Remote work for a foreign company, freelance consulting, gig economy work, selling products online, and unpaid internships at for-profit companies all violate F-2 status. Even one paycheck or one day of work can trigger status violation and future inadmissibility.
04 Plan Ahead Build financial independence within the rules
F-2 spouses should plan for no work income during the F-1 students program. Explore: part-time recreational study (build skills), volunteer at non-profits, prepare for future F-1 or H-4 EAD eligibility. Keep skills current through online courses and certifications.
Overview
For F-1 students planning to bring their spouse and children to the United States, understanding the dependent visa process is essential. This guide covers f2-visa-work-authorization-rules, from initial application through maintaining status and financial planning.
For families from India
Many Indian-cohort families assume remote work for a Bangalore-based employer is fine because it does not "show up" in the US. USCIS audits at H-1B/H-4 transitions routinely catch this. If you must earn, change to F-1 or wait for an H-4 EAD when the spouse hits H-1B.

F-2 dependent is offered a remote contracting role for a UK-based company, paid in GBP to a UK bank account. Allowed?
A Yes — the income is not US-source 
B No — physical presence in the US while working = US employment, even for foreign clients 
C Yes — as long as no US client is involved 
D Only if the company is a charity 
Eligibility Requirements
F-2 eligibility is directly tied to the F-1 student's status. Spouses and unmarried children under 21 may qualify. Requirements include proof of relationship, evidence of the student's valid F-1 status, and comprehensive financial documentation for the entire family.

What is the only path for an F-2 spouse to work legally?
A Apply for an F-2 EAD 
B Change status to F-1 (and use CPT/OPT) or to a work visa like H-1B

Application Process for Dependents
Dependents can apply for visas at the same time as the student or after the student has received theirs. Each dependent needs their own DS-160 confirmation, fee receipt, and interview appointment. Financial documents must show sufficient resources for the entire family.
Rights and Restrictions for F-2 Dependents
The F-2 visa allows spouses and children to live in the US but with limited activities. Spouses cannot work and can only study part-time in non-degree programs. Children can attend US public schools without a separate student visa.
“ F-2 is the strictest "no work" status in US immigration. Even a single paid hour can void the entire family’s plan. 
Financial Planning for Families
F-1 students with dependents should plan for $15,000 to $25,000 in additional annual expenses per dependent. Largest costs are housing, food, and health insurance. Explore on-campus employment and scholarships that consider family circumstances.
The prohibition on F-2 employment and why remote work is included
F-2 dependents are absolutely prohibited from engaging in any form of employment in the United States. This includes not only traditional W-2 employment but also remote work for a company based outside the US, freelance projects, independent contractor arrangements, gig economy jobs (Uber, DoorDash, TaskRabbit), and unpaid positions that the Department of Labor would classify as employment. The rationale is that F-2 status is purely derivative; the F-2 holder’s presence in the US is for family unity, not for economic activity. If a CBP officer or USCIS adjudicator finds evidence of F-2 employment — through social media, tax records, or an I-485 interview — the dependent may be found to have violated status, which can trigger accrual of unlawful presence and ineligibility for future immigration benefits. If the F-2 spouse needs to work, the family must switch the principal’s status to a category that permits dependent employment, or the dependent must obtain their own work-authorized status (e.g., F-1, H-1B, or L-2).
Pathways from F-2 to work-authorized status
An F-2 spouse who wishes to work has several options, depending on qualifications and timing. (1) F-2 to F-1: Apply for admission to a US degree program, obtain a new I-20, and apply for a change of status to F-1 within the US or through consular processing abroad. body:

H-1B Visa Guide Guide

§ Key takeaways
01 H-1B is the main bridge from F-1/OPT to long-term US work — but it is gated by an annual cap and a lottery. 
02 Standard cap is 65,000 + 20,000 US master’s. Selection is random; registration opens each March. 
03 Cap-exempt employers (universities, affiliated non-profits, government research) skip the lottery entirely. 
04 A registered H-1B start date of 1 October triggers the "cap-gap" — F-1 status is auto-extended until then. 
05 Only your employer can file the H-1B petition (Form I-129). You cannot self-petition. 
The process at a glance
01 Year 1 of OPT Find a sponsor early
Begin applying to H-1B sponsors before your post-completion OPT begins. Filter job boards by "H-1B sponsor" or check the USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub.
02 Early March Employer registers you
Your employer creates a USCIS online registration ($10 fee) listing your passport details. Selection results are released by 31 March.
03 April–June Employer files Form I-129
If selected, the employer has a 90-day window to file the full petition with LCA from the Department of Labor, fees, and your evidence (degree, transcripts, passport).
04 June–September Wait for approval
Standard processing runs 2–4 months; premium processing (extra fee) returns a decision in 15 calendar days. Cap-gap protects your F-1 status if your OPT expires in this window.
05 1 October Start H-1B employment
You can begin H-1B work on 1 October of the same year, even if your OPT EAD expired earlier. Your DSO will not issue a new I-20 — your H-1B approval notice (I-797) is your proof of status.
Overview
For F-1 international students, understanding work authorization rules is critical to maintaining lawful status. This comprehensive guide explains h1b-visa-guide-international-students in detail, covering eligibility, application procedures, and compliance obligations.
For students from India
Indian nationals make up roughly 70% of all H-1B selections — but country-of-birth EB green card backlogs run decades. Treat the H-1B as the beginning of a 6-year clock to file an I-140 (EB-2/EB-3), not the end of the process.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
Who is allowed to file an H-1B petition for you?
A You can self-petition once you have a job offer 
B Only a US employer who agrees to sponsor you 
C Your university’s international student office 
D Any licensed US immigration attorney 
Eligibility and Key Requirements
To be eligible, F-1 students must maintain valid immigration status throughout the process. This means full-time enrollment, no unauthorized employment history, and SEVIS compliance. Your DSO plays a crucial role in verifying eligibility and initiating work authorization applications.
For students from China
Chinese applicants face additional 221(g) administrative-processing review for STEM roles in sensitive fields (semiconductors, AI, aerospace). Schedule the visa stamping interview at least 4 weeks before your 1 October start.
Languages: Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) · Cantonese
Application Process and Timelines
The work authorization process involves steps in the correct order. Your DSO recommends you in SEVIS and issues an endorsed I-20. Then compile your application package and submit within the designated window. Track progress through your USCIS online account.
Maintaining Compliance and Reporting
After approval, ongoing compliance is essential. Report address changes within 10 days, stay within authorized hours, and keep your SEVIS record active. For OPT participants, unemployment days count against your authorized period, so track employment status carefully.
Common Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
The most costly mistakes include missing filing deadlines, exceeding unemployment limits, and accepting unauthorized employment. These errors jeopardize your application and F-1 status. Understand rules thoroughly, maintain a compliance calendar, and seek professional guidance.
“ H-1B is not a guarantee — it is a lottery. Plan for the case where you are not selected, every year. 
The H-1B cap, lottery, and registration timeline
The H-1B visa has an annual cap of 65,000 regular visas plus 20,000 reserved for applicants holding a US master’s degree or higher from an accredited US institution. Employers must first register beneficiaries in a pre-lottery registration system, usually in March. USCIS then conducts a randomized lottery to select enough registrations to fill the cap. Selected applicants receive a filing window — typically April to June — during which the employer submits a full petition with supporting documents. The entire process from registration to approval takes four to nine months, and the H-1B start date is October 1 of the same fiscal year at the earliest. If your registration is not selected, you can either use additional OPT time for another lottery attempt, explore cap-exempt H-1B options (universities, nonprofits, government research), or plan alternatives such as O-1, L-1, or day-1 CPT extensions.
Cap-exempt H-1B employers and how they differ
Certain employers are exempt from the H-1B cap: institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations related to or affiliated with such institutions, nonprofit research organizations, and government research organizations. If you secure a job offer from a cap-exempt employer, there is no lottery — the petition can be filed at any time and approved year-round with an October 1 start date or earlier if amended. Cap-exempt petitions are still adjudicated against the same specialty-occupation criteria as cap-subject petitions, so the role must still meet the degree-and-field nexus test. Many cap-exempt employers also hire on a J-1 or O-1 basis for short-term academic roles. § Key takeaways
01 H-4 is the dependent visa for spouses and children under 21 of H-1B (and certain other H-category) workers. 
02 H-4 EAD is available ONLY to H-4 spouses whose H-1B partner has an approved I-140 OR is in AC21 extension territory. 
03 Apply for H-4 EAD via Form I-765 — typical processing 6–10+ months, biometrics often required. 
04 Standard H-4 (no EAD) status forbids all employment, same as F-2 — including remote and freelance work. 
05 H-4 EAD ends when the H-1B principal’s status ends, when the I-140 is revoked, or upon EAD expiry — no auto-renewal. 
The process at a glance
01 Step 1 Confirm H-1B principal eligibility
Your H-1B spouse needs an approved I-140 OR an AC21-extended H-1B (extended past year 6 due to backlogs). Without either, no H-4 EAD path.
02 Step 2 Gather evidence
I-140 approval notice, current H-1B I-797, marriage certificate, your I-94, passport biopage, current H-4 I-797.
03 Step 3 File Form I-765
Category code (c)(26). Online filing preferred. Filing fee + (often) biometrics fee. File concurrently with H-4 extension if relevant.
04 Step 4 Biometrics + processing
Most applicants attend a biometrics appointment. Processing typically 6–10 months as of 2026 — premium processing not available for (c)(26).
05 Step 5 Receive EAD and notify employer
EAD card arrives by mail. Work can begin on the start date listed; document your status with Form I-9 at any new employer.
Overview
H-4 is a dependent classification for certain family members of H-1B workers. Unlike F-2, some H-4 spouses may apply for employment authorization if the H-1B principal meets AC21 or I-140-based criteria. This guide focuses on eligibility, Form I-765 filing, and practical compliance. Always confirm the current USCIS H-4 EAD rules before you quit a job or file.
For families from India
The H-4 EAD is essentially designed for the Indian-cohort backlog — most beneficiaries are Indian-born spouses awaiting decades-long EB-2/EB-3 visa bulletins. Renew the EAD aggressively (180+ days before expiry) and keep employment records continuous to support the eventual I-485.
Languages: English · Hindi · Tamil · Telugu
§ Test your knowledge
Who can apply for H-4 EAD?
A Any H-4 spouse, immediately upon arrival 
B H-4 spouses whose H-1B partner has an approved I-140 OR is on AC21 H-1B extension 
C Only H-4 children, not spouses 
D Anyone with an SSN 
Eligibility Requirements
H-4 status requires a qualifying relationship to an H-1B principal in valid status. For H-4 EAD, the principal generally needs an approved I-140 or H-1B status extended under AC21 past the sixth year. Not every H-4 spouse qualifies for an EAD. Gather marriage evidence, status documents for both spouses, and the principal’s I-140 or AC21 proof before filing I-765.
For families from China
Chinese-cohort H-4 EAD applicants also benefit, though EB queues are shorter than Indian. Be aware: H-4 EAD does not currently cover children — H-4 children must change to F-1 to study full-time after high school and use CPT/OPT separately.
Languages: Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) · Cantonese
§ Test your knowledge
What is the EAD category code for H-4 spouses?
A (a)(5) 
B (c)(26) 
C (c)(33) 
D (c)(9) 
Application Process for Dependents
File Form I-765 with supporting evidence and the correct fee unless exempt. Concurrent filing with H-4 extension packages is common. Premium processing is typically unavailable for H-4 EAD, so plan for long adjudication. Do not work until the EAD card is approved and valid. Keep receipt notices and copies of everything submitted.
§ Test your knowledge
When does H-4 EAD authorisation typically end?
A On the EAD card’s expiry date, OR sooner if the H-1B status or I-140 is revoked 
B After 6 years no matter what 
C On the day the H-4 spouse becomes a US citizen 
D Only when USCIS sends a written termination 
Rights, Work Authorization, and Limits for H-4 Dependents
Without an EAD, H-4 spouses generally cannot work. Study may be possible depending on the program and status. H-4 status ends if the H-1B principal falls out of status. Coordinate travel so both spouses re-enter with valid visas and supporting approval notices. Report address changes as required.
“ H-4 EAD is the prize that comes after the I-140 — months of waiting, then years of work flexibility. Plan accordingly. 
Financial Planning for Families
Budget filing fees, potential gap months without dual income, and health insurance for the family while the EAD is pending. Maintain emergency savings because H-4 EAD timelines are unpredictable. This is educational guidance — complex AC21 or consular issues need a licensed attorney.
Who can apply for H-4 EAD and what Form I-765 requires
Certain H-4 spouses of H-1B workers may apply for employment authorization using Form I-765 if the H-1B principal is the beneficiary of an approved I-140 or has H-1B status extended under AC21 beyond the sixth year. Not every H-4 spouse qualifies. The application package typically includes proof of the marriage, proof of H-4 status, proof of the H-1B principal’s status and I-140 or AC21 basis, passport identity pages, and the correct filing fee or fee waiver request if eligible. There is no premium processing for H-4 EAD in most cases, so plan for multi-month adjudication. Work only after the EAD is approved and valid — filing alone does not authorize employment.
Travel, job changes, and coordination with the H-1B principal
H-4 status depends on the H-1B principal remaining in valid status. If the principal loses the job or falls out of status, H-4 and any H-4 EAD can be affected. Report address changes, keep copies of all I-797 notices, and align travel plans so both spouses re-enter with the correct visas and supporting documents. The process at a glance
01 Understand Requirements Know your mandatory health insurance obligations
Most US universities require F-1 and J-1 students to carry health insurance that meets minimum coverage standards: at least $100k per accident, $50k per illness, $25k medical evacuation, and $10k repatriation. University plans cost $1,500-$4,000 per year but are the simplest option. Private international student plans ($500-$2,000/year) may be cheaper but must meet your schools waiver criteria. Compare deductibles, coverage limits, prescription benefits, and network access before deciding.

Ensure your plan covers: doctor visits, hospitalization, emergency care, prescription drugs, mental health services, and pre-existing conditions after a waiting period. Some plans exclude sports injuries or adventure activities. Read the policy details carefully before purchasing.
04 Plan for Gaps Handle coverage transitions and gaps
If you graduate, change status, or travel, ensure continuous coverage. OPT students often lose university coverage and need private plans. Short gaps (under 3 months) may be acceptable, but longer gaps can affect future visa applications. Consider catastrophic coverage as a minimum.

Most US universities require all international students to carry health insurance that meets specific minimum standards. body:
